source.title: Neuroplasticity and Corruption in Model Mechanisms: A Case Study Of Indirect Object Identification
source.authors: V. Chhabra; Ding Zhu; M. Khalili

record.tranche_reason: The study applies IOI circuit-discovery and evaluation procedures based on the original work, including path patching, knockout, and circuit faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation, to GPT-2-small fine-tuning checkpoints. It also examines backup-head self-repair.
record.gate_note: The study reports circuit results for clean IOI fine-tuning and self-repair, which are included below. It does not report a comparison of circuit-discovery methods. Its corrupted-data experiments intentionally alter IOI behavior; those induced behaviors are not treated as evidence about uninduced IOI performance. The paper cites the original circuit's 87% faithfulness result rather than reproducing that result, so it is not recorded as a row. It does not report outcome differences by IOI template or name order.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the original path-patching and knockout procedure on new GPT-2-small checkpoints: IOI fine-tunes at 1 to 100 epochs, plus general fine-tunes in Appendix E. It reports circuit faithfulness and minimality, the head classes found, and backup and self-repair behaviour. This bears on V3 (training checkpoints) and V2. It does not re-derive the pretrained 26-head circuit, so V1 is not directly retested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also stress that clean fine-tuning amplifies existing IOI mechanisms without introducing novel ones, partly by adding heads that replicate existing roles. Corrupted fine-tuning alters localized circuit components, and clean retraining restores the original mechanisms (neuroplasticity).
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original IOI circuit-discovery approach, including path patching and knockout, and evaluates faithfulness, completeness, and minimality. Applies it to fine-tuned GPT-2-small checkpoints and studies corruption and retraining rather than reproducing the original pretrained-model circuit alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on corrupted IOI data alters only circuit components: name movers lose IO copying, S-inhibition heads change, and negative name movers flip to suppressing S. Retraining on clean data restores the original mechanisms (post-reversal faithfulness 95%/96%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The IOI circuit components are the locus of task corruption under toxic fine-tuning and re-form after clean retraining.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The IOI experiments concern GPT-2-small only. The study uses task-specific fine-tuning, so its high IOI scores are not evidence that an unmodified model shows the same behavior. Some circuit-evaluation and self-repair results are only shown in figures without numerical values. The authors note that broader architectures and tasks require further study.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Corrupted-data performance changes were not cataloged as evidence for the ordinary IOI mechanism because the study deliberately induces those changes through corrupted fine-tuning.

untested.parts: The pretrained GPT-2-small circuit is not re-derived or re-evaluated. The study cites the original 87% rather than reproducing it.
No other model families or sizes are tested for IOI. Reuse of IOI components for other tasks is not tested; the Greater-Than analysis is a separate circuit.
Only the original path-patching method is used for IOI. There is no comparison of methods, ablation types or metrics.
Ablation type, metric and prompt distribution are not varied.
Results are not broken down by template, name order or number of names.

missing.what: Circuit faithfulness in non-IOI-fine-tuned GPT-2 variants: GPT2-dolly 98%, math_gpt2 96.8%, GPT2-WikiText 100%, TinyStories+IOI 97.6%. These checkpoints were not trained for IOI, so this is the cleanest V3 evidence.
Backup head L10H10 takes on the name-mover role after 3 epochs; its logit attribution rises from 0.4 to 1.8.
Ablating head groups (S-inhibition, previous token, induction, duplicate token) in the original vs. the fine-tuned model, which shows a larger effect after fine-tuning.
MLPs other than MLP0 contribute little in the fine-tuned circuits, matching the original.

record.verdict_notes: I chose T3 over T1: the method is the original's, but the subjects are fine-tuned checkpoints, and most are deliberately trained on IOI itself. That is a deliberate intervention, so its high faithfulness says little about uninduced checkpoints; Table 3 is the better V3 evidence. The 'faithfulness' metric is a performance ratio, not the original's absolute difference, so it is not comparable to the original 87%. No V1 verdict is given because no row measures the pretrained circuit.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates circuits discovered after task-specific fine-tuning, not the exact pretrained 26-head circuit as a whole; the exact head count and all seven classes' roles in the unmodified pretrained model are not newly established here.
The detailed backup/self-repair results are for GPT-2-small and do not establish that backup heads take over in other models or sizes.

Only GPT-2-small is tested for IOI. Other model sizes and architectures are not tested. Although the paper also studies a separate Greater-Than circuit, it does not test reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
The study does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics to determine whether they recover the same circuit.
It does not systematically vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution to test evaluation sensitivity.

The IOI dataset has 15 templates and names drawn from a list of 100, but results are not separated by template, name order, or number of names; the study does not test whether the same mechanism works across those variants.

relation.reason: The study directly evaluates preservation of IOI mechanisms across checkpoints and compensation after name-mover ablation.

tranche.reason: Rediscovered IOI circuits and backup behaviour are evaluated in new fine-tuned checkpoints. The discovery procedure follows the original approach, but the tested checkpoint setting is new.

source_check.notes: Table 1 reports epoch-50 faithfulness as 99.7%, although 22.75/22.87 is approximately 99.48%; R6 accurately copies the source. Appendix E also reports circuit metrics for instruction-tuned GPT2-dolly, without supplying a complete head-class decomposition.

statements.correction: Table 1: additional-component contributions 0.35–2.2; Section 4.1: new components replicate existing mechanisms; L10H10 becomes a name mover after 3 epochs; V3 does not require fixed head indices.
statements.problem: The factual findings are supported, but changing head membership does not limit V3's claim of preserved head classes and functional roles.
